data.what_done: Traced why subagent sessions can show the primary agent in the UI despite Task metadata showing the subagent name.
data.approach_taken: Inspected TUI state management and prompt initialization logic tied to session changes.
data.challenges_faced: The mismatch is visual/UI-level rather than in TaskTool itself, so needed to locate where the agent display is sourced.
data.how_solved: Found that local agent state excludes subagents and the session-change sync tries to set a subagent name, which fails silently and leaves the primary agent active.
data.reasoning: UI derives the current agent from a list that filters out subagents; therefore, even when the subagent session’s last user message references a subagent, the active agent shown remains the last primary agent.
next_steps: Decide whether to allow subagent agents in the local UI list for child sessions.
Alternatively, add a read-only subagent label in subagent sessions and keep selection limited to primary agents.
